text: Diagnosis in adults follows the Rotterdam criteria, now specified in more evidence-based detail. Two of three features are required: ovulatory dysfunction, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology, once other causes have been excluded.

text: When a woman has both irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism, which covers roughly seven in ten cases, neither an ultrasound nor an AMH blood test is needed to make the diagnosis.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: Polycystic ovarian morphology is defined on transvaginal ultrasound as 20 or more follicles of 2 to 9 mm diameter in at least one ovary. Ovarian volume of 10 mL or more can be used as an alternative measure. If only abdominal ultrasound is available, ovarian volume is the preferred measure.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: The 2023 recommendations changed the follicle number per ovary used for polycystic ovarian morphology to 20 or more, and highlight follicle number per ovary as an important ultrasound marker.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: AMH correlates strongly with antral follicle count, so the 2023 guideline allows an AMH level as an alternative way to estimate polycystic ovarian morphology in adults. AMH has no single cut-off; reference values depend on the assay and on age.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: AMH testing is advised only in adults because AMH levels overlap between women with and without PCOS, especially in adolescents.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: Ultrasound or AMH should be used together with exclusion of other causes. Neither is a stand-alone diagnostic test. TSH and prolactin screening is recommended, along with clinical review for rarer conditions such as Cushing's syndrome.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: In adolescents the diagnosis needs both ovulatory dysfunction and clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, plus exclusion of other causes; ultrasound morphology alone should not be used to label an adolescent.
provenance: paraphrase of retrieved source content; not verbatim

text: The 2023 guideline was approved by the Australian NHMRC in July 2023 and rests on 52 systematic reviews, 77 evidence-based and 54 consensus recommendations.
